mission: The Ruusan Reformations question — what the galaxy was told they were for. Ben answers honestly. Sera goes very still. Each survivor grieves the displacement differently. Kael asks about his homeworld; the database returns nothing, and something behind his face changes.
why_now: Before the group can function under pressure, the three have to register what a thousand years has cost them. Ben has to see them as people before the Corridor tests the coalition.
conflict: Sera absorbs the Reformations answer in silence. Torin's adaptation is so easy that Ben notices the ease itself. Kael watches the room without entering it. The common area becomes smaller the longer they all sit in it.
turning_point: Kael asks what happened to the Sith world he was taken from. Ben searches and finds nothing — the planet was too small for surviving records. Kael's expression does not change, but the line of his shoulders does.
opening_hook: Sera asks about the Ruusan Reformations — what the galaxy was told they were for. Ben answers honestly. She goes very still.
closing_hook: Torin catches Ben's eye across the common area and nods — the nod of a commander acknowledging a subordinate who handled something difficult well. Ben is not sure if he should be reassured or concerned that Torin is already thinking in command structure.
emotional_trajectory: Awkward information exchange -> raw grief (Kael's moment) -> fragile group empathy

stakes.personal: Ben seeing the human cost of what was done to these people
stakes.interpersonal: Building real connection vs. mission-focused alliance
stakes.external: The survivors' displacement is also an intelligence gap — they do not understand the modern galaxy's politics

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — common area, cramped and intimate
sensory_details: Modern field rations that taste like nothing the survivors remember; the datapad scrolling a galactic history none of them can read fast enough; Kael's silence taking up more of the small space than his body does
action_beats: Ben pulls up a galactic history archive on the datapad and slides it across the table to Sera
Kael asks about his homeworld and Ben searches the database — the screen returning nothing, the planet too small for surviving records
Torin nods across the common area with a commander's acknowledgment that Ben can't tell is approval or assessment
promises_planted: Kael's detachment is a defense mechanism (PP09)
notes: Kael's moment about his homeworld is small and load-bearing — plants his arc. He is not detached because he does not care; he is detached because caring cost him everything and nobody ever asked. Let the empty database entry do what no line of dialogue could. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, narrate Kael's psychology or name the defence mechanism. He observes, Desh senses without naming, Torin mediates, Sera absorbs. The reader registers Kael's cost through what the screen does not say. Voice: Allston-brief dialogue, Stover-interior beat permitted only on Ben's recognition of Kael's silence. Prior-EU onboarding — if Mara or Vestara surfaces in the history scroll, each gets one grounding phrase at most, no paragraph.
